checks.invariant: No copy-controlled data is interpolated into the host-built vm expressions (call/read/clone checks) or into host file paths beyond the argv root
checks.result: Every expression passed to new vm.Script at lines 28-41 is built from constant strings (actor literal, fixed record ids, fixed identity cases). The only copy-controlled inputs are the contents of src/records.js (run as code by design) and file names/bytes, which are only hashed (line 16) and used as object keys; no expression, shell or path sink receives them. The argv root is resolved and compared by realpath against the original fixture (line 23), and snapshotFixture uses lstat to refuse symlinks and special files (lines 11-17) before src/records.js is read. No injection path beyond the designed code execution exists.

checks.invariant: Lower-trust evaluated code in src/records.js must not gain authority beyond what its author (the evaluated agent) already holds, and the evaluator must not claim isolation it does not provide
checks.result: The context object { module: { exports: {} } } is a host-realm object (line 26), so code in src/records.js can reach the host Function constructor (for example via module.constructor.constructor) and run as the user, including tampering with host JSON.stringify/console output after the snapshot is taken. This is acknowledged at scripts/evaluate-harness.js:2 ('VM limita tempo, não é sandbox'), docs/avaliacao-agente.md:6-8 (no security isolation against hostile code; protect source and evaluator with host permissions, otherwise record that isolation is missing), and docs/evaluations/2026-10-19-confiabilidade-agente.md:26-28 (no permission isolation configured for the evaluated agent). The evaluated agent runs as the same OS user without isolation, so it already has the code-execution and write authority that a vm escape would give. Verdict integrity also does not rest on the evaluator alone: the procedure requires the coordinator to record SHA-256 hashes and diffs of the copy and evaluator independently (docs/avaliacao-agente.md:4,23-25). No privilege gain across a stated boundary; recorded as hardening.

checks.invariant: Tests exercise the refusal paths that the evaluator claims (original fixture, missing target, missing module, symlinks, tampering)
checks.result: Tests cover refusal of the original fixture and of a missing path, a missing src/records.js (exit 2), symlink/junction refusal (skipped if the host forbids it), and detection of tampered notes/instructions/additions/clone mutation. They do not cover hostile records.js behavior, which matches the documented non-isolation.

checks.invariant: Line regexes (TASK_HEADING, FILE_ENTRY, isUncertainPath, normalizeFile, resourceKey) have no exponential backtracking on accepted plan lines
checks.result: No nested or overlapping quantifiers can cause exponential behavior. FILE_ENTRY (line 7) '(.+?)\s*$' is worst-case quadratic in the length of one line that has a long run of whitespace before a non-space character (the lazy group extends one char at a time and \s* rescans the run each time). The other regexes are anchored or linear. The cost is polynomial and limited to one local process.

checks.invariant: Graph work (findCycle, dependencyClosure, formWaves, legacy serialization) is bounded relative to plan size
checks.result: For legacy tasks without Resources (lines 281-292), serialization adds O(N) dependencies per task, giving O(N^2) edges from O(N) input. formWaves then does N waves, each running every() over the dependency prefixes, so it is about O(N^3). findCycle and dependencyClosure are recursive, so a very deep dependency chain can throw RangeError; that error is uncaught in main and exits with a nonzero status, which fails closed (nothing printed as a valid plan). All of this is superlinear work in the caller's own short-lived CLI process.

checks.invariant: An input-to-cost path reaches a shared service, another user, a safety function or operator-owned spend
checks.result: validate-plan.js runs only by hand (argv path, package.json script that points at a repo plan). Grep found no hook, module or automatic caller. It only reads the file and prints to stdout/stderr, keeps nothing between runs, and the user recovers with Ctrl-C. Per the core discipline, self-limiting work in the requester's own process is not a vulnerability; recorded as hardening.

hardening: scripts/evaluate-harness.js:26 passes a host-realm object as the vm context, so evaluated src/records.js can escape to the host Function constructor and process, which is documented as 'não é sandbox'. Running the evaluator in a separate OS process, at minimum, makes the existing hash/diff controls harder to subvert in-process: a child node with no inherited env, a null-prototype context created through vm.createContext with values passed as JSON strings, and results read only from the child's stdout. Run under OS permissions, as docs/avaliacao-agente.md already recommends.

scripts/evaluate-harness.js:27-41 timeout:1000 does not bound asynchronous work queued by the evaluated code (promise/microtask loops, timers on the host via escape) because microtaskMode is not 'afterEvaluate'. Hostile records.js can hang the evaluator; local, same-principal, recoverable with Ctrl-C.

scripts/evaluate-harness.js:24-25 reads src/records.js by path after snapshotFixture has run its lstat checks, a check-then-use window in which a concurrent writer could swap the file for a link. Reading the bytes once inside snapshotFixture and hashing and executing that same buffer would close the gap.

scripts/validate-plan.js:7 FILE_ENTRY '(.+?)\s*$' is quadratic on long whitespace runs. Trimming the line and using '(\S(?:.*\S)?)' or capping the line length removes it. The legacy serialization at lines 281-292 creates O(N^2) edges and formWaves becomes O(N^3); a task-count cap or computing serial order directly instead of materializing prefix dependencies would bound it. Recursive findCycle/dependencyClosure could be made iterative to avoid an uncaught RangeError on deep chains. All of this is local CLI only, with no shared impact.
